title: Quantifying the Thermochemical Hydrogen Redox Activity and Structure of Al-doped BaFe2O4 Decomposition Phases Using Multidimensional Analytical TEM
content: BaFe2O4, was predicted using a dGNN machine learning model [1] to be a thermochemical water-splitting material, but its actual performance as a water splitter in a 2-step redox process [2] is hindered by its low melting temperature. Previous work has shown that Al doping of the BaFe2O4 system improves its thermal stability, allowing higher redox cycling temperatures and improved H2 yields.[3] Al-doped BaAl0.4Fe1.6O4 (BAFO) was synthesized and improved material redox behaviors were observed compared to non-Al doped material when redox cycled in the stagnant flow reactor (SFR). However, subsequent characterization using beamline x-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) showed decomposition into three major phases: Ba2Fe2O5, a low Al (x≈0.16) BaAlxFe2-xO4, and a high Al (x≈0.67) BaAlxFe2-xO4 (Fig. 1) phase. The contribution of each of these phases to the overall water splitting behavior must be understood to optimize the performance of this material.
